sentences.text: An inductor consists of a coil of conducting wire wound around a core of air, iron, or ferrite.
When current flows through the coil, a magnetic field builds up around it.
By Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law, any change in current induces an opposing voltage: v = L × (di / dt).
An inductor resists changes in current.
In a steady-state DC circuit where current is constant (di/dt = 0), an ideal inductor has zero voltage drop and acts as a Short Circuit.
Inductive Kick (Flyback Spike): Abruptly disconnecting an energized inductor creates a dangerous reverse voltage spike ( v = -L di over dt is much greater than V supply ) that destroys transistors.
A reverse-biased flyback diode must be placed anti-parallel across the coil to clamp the spike to V clamp is approximately V supply + 0.7 V .
